target: Decide whether Cslib/Logics/Propositional/Tableau/Intuitionistic.lean should declare its Scheme sibling, and surface the prevailing barrel convention under Cslib/Logics/
summary: VERDICT: oversight, not design. Fix is ONE line added to Cslib/Logics/Propositional/Tableau/Intuitionistic.lean; Cslib.lean must NOT be touched. Two premises in the task description are falsified. (1) Cslib.lean does not import Scheme 'instead of' the sub-barrel — it imports EVERY module: exactly 702 `public import` lines against exactly 702 .lean files under Cslib/. It is generated by `lake exe mk_all --module` and lists parent and child alike everywhere, including the five siblings the sub-barrel DOES declare, so line 636 carries zero information about intent. (2) The suggestion to 'consider dropping the direct line from Cslib.lean' would BREAK CI: CONTRIBUTING.md's Imports section states there is a test that Cslib.lean imports all files, and the next mk_all run would re-add it. Surveyed all 26 barrels under Cslib/Logics/ (every X.lean with a sibling X/ dir, compared against that dir's direct children): 13 EXHAUSTIVE, 13 PARTIAL — so exhaustiveness is NOT a repo-wide convention and cannot be asserted as one; two barrels (Semantics/Algebra.lean 0/29, Syntax/SubformulaClosure.lean 0/2) declare none of their children. ORGANISATION.md's only barrel language is descriptive prose (lines 57, 198), not a rule; CONTRIBUTING.md says nothing about sub-barrels. The decisive comparison is therefore LOCAL: among the three tableau siblings, Classical.lean declares its full dependency chain (4/4, including links redundant transitively), Minimal.lean is terminus-only (1/3), and Intuitionistic.lean declares its full chain MINUS ONE INTERIOR LINK (5/6). A file written in the declare-the-whole-chain style that skips exactly one interior link is an omission, not a third style. Verified true chain from each file's own imports: Rules -> Expansion -> Soundness -> (Minimal.Soundness) -> Scheme -> Completeness -> DecisionProcedure, so Scheme sits strictly between Soundness and Completeness. Chronology confirms oversight: Intuitionistic.lean's 5-import list predates Scheme.lean's existence (043e8db9); Scheme.lean was added 2026-06-27 (d4714ecd); commit cc5a0c04 on 2026-06-28 added module headers to the barrels AND to Scheme.lean in the same change but never revisited the aggregator's membership list — its message even classifies Scheme.lean as 'the content file' alongside 'the 5 aggregator files'. No deliberate-exclusion evidence exists anywhere (no comment, no docstring note, no ORGANISATION.md entry, no commit message). The change is provably inert: Intuitionistic.lean already imports Completeness, and Completeness.lean:11 already carries `public import ...Scheme`, so the transitive import-graph closure is LITERALLY UNCHANGED — zero new edges, zero cycle risk, and critically ZERO build-cost impact (Scheme.olean is already a prerequisite of the sub-barrel, so the expensive Scheme module is not pulled into any new target; this directly addresses the task's cost warning). Shake exposure assessed as nil: Intuitionistic.lean is absent from the 23-path scripts/shake-residue-baseline.txt, all 15 exhaustive barrels consist entirely of unused pure re-export public imports and none is flagged, and --keep-implied is precisely the flag preventing removal of an import implied by another (the exact shape of the new line). No lake build was run, per the task constraint; the survey was fully static.

artifacts.summary: Full 26-barrel convention survey, dependency-chain verification, git chronology, shake assessment, and the exact one-line change with its position rationale

decisions_made: Recommended adding `public import Cslib.Logics.Propositional.Tableau.Intuitionistic.Scheme` to the sub-barrel between the existing Soundness and Completeness lines — the dependency position, matching the file's existing bottom-up ordering and Classical.lean's ordering. Explicitly not alphabetical: no sibling sub-barrel is alphabetical, only the machine-generated Cslib.lean.

Explicitly REJECTED the task description's suggestion to consider dropping line 636 from Cslib.lean. That file is mk_all-generated and CI-enforced exhaustive (702 imports / 702 files); removing the line breaks the imports test and mk_all would re-add it.

Explicitly REJECTED recording a 'deliberately excluded' note as the alternative resolution. Scheme is public API — the parametric core (IntMinScheme, intScheme, minScheme, truthLemma, openBranch_countermodel) cited from Minimal/Completeness.lean, Minimal/DecisionProcedure.lean, Int/MinDecidability.lean and six test files — so exclusion has no defensible reading.

Did NOT recommend normalizing the other 12 partial barrels found by the survey (notably Semantics/Algebra.lean 0/29 and Modal/Metalogic.lean 5/14). Partial barrels are widespread and several are large and possibly intentional; bundling them would convert a one-line hygiene fix into an unscoped refactor. Flagged as a separate optional task.

Declined to assert 'sub-barrels must be exhaustive' as a project convention despite it being the convenient justification — the survey measured 13/26, and two barrels declare zero children. The recommendation rests instead on the local Classical-vs-Intuitionistic style match plus the git chronology.

Ran no lake build at all, honouring the task's cost constraint, and stated the one residual uncertainty openly rather than asserting it away: the shake verdict is static (precedent + flag semantics + baseline absence) and should be confirmed with `bash scripts/check-shake-residue.sh --list` during implementation once a built tree exists.
